memoryLayout.concept: Facility code and card number bit formats

beginnerExplanation: HID Prox cards are commonly used for building access and are usually LF, not NFC.

cardProfile.name: HID Prox / H10301
cardProfile.description: HID Prox is a low-frequency access credential family. A common H10301 decode exposes a facility code, card number and raw ID, not personal details.
limitations: Facility code and card number identify a credential but do not prove who owns it
Access rights normally live in the access-control system, not on the card
recommendedNextSteps: Record facility code and card number
Add Known by You context such as owner or location
cardProfile.meaning: This card normally carries a credential number. The door system decides what that number means and whether it is allowed access.
notVisibleReasons: HID Prox credentials normally do not store a person name on the card.
Validity dates and permissions are usually stored in the access-control database.
A raw ID is not the same thing as an identity document.

faqs.question: Why do I not see a name?
faqs.answer: HID Prox cards normally expose an identifier. Names and permissions are usually stored in the access-control system.

faqs.question: Is this NFC?
faqs.answer: No. HID Prox is normally 125 kHz LF RFID, not NFC.
